question: Should OpenClaw accept optional `currentTokenCount` plus these token-budget helper exports as a stable public ContextEngine/plugin SDK contract now, or fold the token-accounting signal into the broader assemble metadata RFC at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82137?
rationale: The PR is an additive public plugin API change that third-party context engines may compile against, while adjacent assemble metadata and trust-boundary questions remain open.

options.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Repairs
options.body: Approve `currentTokenCount` as a separate backward-compatible API after the two patch blockers are fixed and live behavior proof is posted.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Metadata RFC
options.body: Pause this PR and design token counts together with provenance, internal-event, and live-turn metadata in the broader assemble contract.

options.title: Keep Helpers Private For Now
options.body: Allow internal token-count plumbing but remove the SDK helper exports until maintainers settle the permanent public helper surface.

recommendation.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Repairs
recommendation.body: Approve `currentTokenCount` as a separate backward-compatible API after the two patch blockers are fixed and live behavior proof is posted.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned on the PR, authored the current head commits, and have the strongest recent history on the affected context-engine budget path.
